title: Step 10 - Answer
section: 20. Boss Level Challenge 2 - The Simon Game
summary: Answer page for the last Simon step. The solution download (Course Resources button, top left of the lecture screen) is the finished app, with each challenge step labelled in comments; the notes below reconstruct the complete game.js with the Step 10 startOver() logic.

concepts.heading: How to use the answer download
points: The download is the whole finished project, not just Step 10, so it doubles as the reference for every earlier step. Each step is marked with a comment so you can jump to the part you are checking.
It is reached from the Course Resources button in the top-left corner of the lecture player.
Your version does not have to match line for line. Different code that produces the same behaviour (same sequence logic, sounds, animations and restart) counts as a correct solution.

concepts.heading: Step 10 solution: startOver()
points: startOver() reassigns the three globals: level = 0, gamePattern = [], started = false.
It is called at the end of the else branch in checkAnswer(), after the wrong sound, the red game-over flash and the 'Game Over, Press Any Key to Restart' heading.
Because started is false again, the next key press passes the if (!started) check in the keyboard listener, which sets the heading, calls nextSequence() and flips started back to true.
nextSequence() clears userClickedPattern and increments level from 0 to 1, so the new game starts cleanly.

concepts.heading: How the finished game fits together (all ten steps)
points: State: buttonColours = ['red','blue','green','yellow'] (lookup table for random picks), gamePattern (computer's sequence), userClickedPattern (player's clicks this round), started (game in progress?), level (round number).
Start (Step 7): $(document).keypress(...) runs once per key press; the started flag makes sure only the first press after load or after a game over starts a game.

New round (Steps 2-3): nextSequence() resets userClickedPattern, increments level and updates #level-title, picks Math.floor(Math.random() * 4) (an integer 0-3), looks up that colour, pushes it onto gamePattern, flashes the button with .fadeIn(100).fadeOut(100).fadeIn(100) and plays its sound.

Player input (Steps 4-6): $('.btn').click(...) reads the clicked div's id with $(this).attr('id'), pushes it onto userClickedPattern, plays the matching sound and calls animatePress() to add the .pressed class for 100 ms.

Checking (Step 8): checkAnswer(userClickedPattern.length - 1) passes the index of the most recent click. If gamePattern and userClickedPattern agree at that index the click was right; if the player has now matched the whole sequence (lengths equal), nextSequence() is scheduled with setTimeout(..., 1000).
Game over (Step 9): on a mismatch, play wrong.mp3, add the game-over class to body and remove it after 200 ms, and change the heading text.
Restart (Step 10): startOver() resets the state so the keyboard listener can start again.
Helpers: playSound(name) builds new Audio('sounds/' + name + '.mp3') and calls .play(); animatePress(currentColour) adds then removes the pressed class via setTimeout.

concepts.heading: Reference repo differences
points: (Extra) The reference repo names the script script.js and listens with $(document).keydown(...); the course project uses game.js. keydown and keypress both work here; keydown also fires for keys like Shift and arrows, and keypress is deprecated in modern browsers.

(Extra) Bug in the reference nextSequence(): it calls playSound(randomNumber), which requests sounds/0.mp3 to sounds/3.mp3 (files that do not exist), so the computer's flash is silent. The call should be playSound(randomChosenColour).
(Extra) The reference index.html has a typo, <div lass="row"> instead of class="row", and a personal footer; both are stripped from these notes.

task.name: Simon Step 10 answer: restart the game
task.starting_point: Your game.js after attempting Step 10, plus the finished solution project from Course Resources.
task.goal: Confirm the restart works and compare your full script with the finished version.
steps: Download the solution from the Course Resources button and unzip it.
Find the Step 10 comment and compare startOver() with yours: three assignments, level 0, empty gamePattern, started false.
Check that startOver() is called inside the else branch of checkAnswer().
Play several games in a row to verify each restart begins at Level 1 with a single flash.
Optionally walk through the other labelled steps to tidy any earlier differences.
task.expected_result: A complete, replayable Simon game: key press to start, growing random sequence with sounds and flashes, red flash plus game-over heading on a mistake, and a fresh game on the next key press.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 20 - Boss Level Challenge 2 - The Simon Game/script.js

pitfalls: Treating a different-but-working solution as wrong; matching behaviour is what counts.
Copying the reference repo's playSound(randomNumber) line, which silences the computer's turn because no numbered mp3 files exist.
Comparing whole arrays with === (gamePattern === userClickedPattern is always false for two different arrays); compare one index at a time as checkAnswer() does.
Calling nextSequence() immediately instead of after a delay, so the next flash overlaps the player's last click.

gaps_and_ideas: Blurb for a new 'Simon game: finished build' project lesson: assemble state, a start listener, sequence generation, click handling, answer checking, game over and restart into one working game.

Tasks: (1) write nextSequence() with the random pick and flash; (2) handle clicks and push to userClickedPattern; (3) write checkAnswer() comparing the latest index; (4) add game-over feedback; (5) add startOver().
Starter code: the HTML grid of four coloured divs, styles.css with .pressed and .game-over, and a game.js skeleton with the five global variables and empty functions marked by step comments.

Interactive demo: a step-through mode that pauses after each event and highlights which function ran and how the arrays changed, plus a 'bug hunt' toggle that swaps in the playSound(randomNumber) mistake for learners to diagnose.
